intents.statement: Provide descriptive `alt` text for all **content images**.

intents.statement: **Use only approved tokens** — always use the design tokens specified in the component guidance, never raw hex values or custom tokens.
**Clarity and accessibility** — all Canopy colour combinations meet or exceed WCAG 2.2 AA contrast standards.
**Consistency** — apply the same colour roles across all products; never mix colour modes within a single view (card, panel, content area, or page).
**Favour neutral backgrounds** — use off-white or white as the default background; white space is a key brand device.
**Flat design language** — gradients and shadows are not permitted.
lead with `blue` — it is the default mode for all Canopy products and experiences.
use only the approved Canopy colour tokens specified in the component guidance — never invent your own or use raw colour values.

capabilities.description: Writing and tone of voice guidance for Canopy applications. Trigger when writing UI text, labels, error messages, headings, button text, or any copy in an Angular project using Canopy.

intents.statement: **Bright** — bring intelligence and energy; demonstrate expertise in accessible language.
**Calm** — keep it simple, concise, and confident; let the facts speak.
**Real** — be down to earth, warm, and transparent; write like you speak.
**Lead with the benefit** — tell users what's in it for them early on.
**Understand your audience** — explain acronyms, avoid jargon, write at reading age 9.
**Active, not passive** — "The system updated your address" not "Your address has been updated".
**Draw pictures with words** — prefer concrete objects over abstract ideas.
**Structure your thoughts** — order messages logically before you write.
**Edit and simplify** — cut unnecessary words; avoid long sentences.
**Use "you"** — prefer "you" over "we" to involve the reader.
**Write like you speak** — use contractions ("You're" not "You are"), avoid clichés.
Set expectations — titles should describe what the content contains and how it helps.
Keep titles short and actionable: "How do I update my address online".
Use descriptive verbs: **Accept**, **Create**, **Delete**, **Save**, **Update**.
Avoid vague terms: **Yes**, **No**, **OK**, **Click here**.
Use words that describe the destination or action: "Update my address", "View my policy documents".
Never write "click here" or "find out more" as link text.
Be specific about what went wrong and what the user needs to do to fix it.
Use active, direct language without blame.
Keep each paragraph short and to the point.
Break content into bite-sized chunks; users scan rather than read.
Use subheadings, bullet points, and whitespace to aid scanning.
focus on the customer's goal before writing.
use words that customers themselves would use.
use active, confident language: "you should", "we recommend".
keep body text scannable with short paragraphs and subheadings.
